issue.title: [autocomplete] Fix popup input FormData submission

labels.name: component: autocomplete
labels.description: Changes related to the autocomplete component.

issue.body:
Fixes #4724.

## Summary

- keep popup-positioned Autocomplete inputs from owning the native form `name`
- let the persistent hidden input submit `selectionMode="none"` values when the input is inside a `Positioner`
- preserve outside and inline Autocomplete native submission through the visible input
- add regression coverage for popup, inline, and default-value-before-open native `FormData` paths

## Root cause

`Autocomplete.Root` delegates to `AriaCombobox` with `selectionMode="none"`, so the submitted field value is the input value rather than a selected value. Base UI `Form.onFormSubmit` could read that value through the Field registry, but native `FormData` only reads named DOM controls.

When the input is rendered inside the popup, the visible input is transient and can unmount after selection. The persistent hidden input existed, but it was unnamed for `selectionMode="none"`, so native `FormData` had no stable named control to read from.

This complements #4687, which fixed the adjacent Combobox popup-input Field registration path.

## Validation

- `pnpm test:jsdom AutocompleteRoot --no-watch -t "native FormData"`
- `pnpm test:chromium AutocompleteRoot --no-watch -t "native FormData"`
- `pnpm test:jsdom ComboboxRoot --no-watch -t "submits when input inside popup renders a field-aware input"`
- `pnpm test:chromium ComboboxRoot --no-watch -t "submits when input inside popup renders a field-aware input"`
- `pnpm test:jsdom AutocompleteRoot --no-watch`
- `pnpm typescript`
- `pnpm prettier`
- `pnpm eslint`
- `git diff --check`

comments.body:
The names here get a bit confusing.

`inputInsidePositioner` fixes the immediate ambiguity, but it adds a second boolean next to `inputInsidePopup`, which sounds similar. (To be fair, its existing meaning is already broader than the name suggests (`hasPositionerParent || inline`) which should possibly be refactored later). The two similar-sounding names makes this hard to reason about because one flag is about focus/layout behavior and the new one is really about native form ownership.

Could we keep `inputInsidePopup` unchanged to reduce how much gets changed in this PR, but rename the new state to the concept it controls?

```ts
inputOwnsFormValue: selectionMode === 'none' && !hasPositionerParent,
```

Then the hidden input branch reads:

```ts
const hiddenInputOwnsNoneValue =
  !inputOwnsFormValue ||
  // Before the popup input mounts, trigger-control comboboxes still need
  // the persistent hidden input to own native form submission.
  (!inline && triggerElement != null && inputElement == null);
```

> The names here get a bit confusing.
> 
> `inputInsidePositioner` fixes the immediate ambiguity, but it adds a second boolean next to `inputInsidePopup`, which sounds similar. (To be fair, its existing meaning is already broader than the name suggests (`hasPositionerParent || inline`) which should possibly be refactored later). The two similar-sounding names makes this hard to reason about because one flag is about focus/layout behavior and the new one is really about native form ownership.
> 
> Could we keep `inputInsidePopup` unchanged to reduce how much gets changed in this PR, but rename the new state to the concept it controls?
> 
> ```ts
> inputOwnsFormValue: selectionMode === 'none' && !hasPositionerParent,
> ```
> 
> Then the hidden input branch reads:
> 
> ```ts
> const hiddenInputOwnsNoneValue =
>   !inputOwnsFormValue ||
>   // Before the popup input mounts, trigger-control comboboxes still need
>   // the persistent hidden input to own native form submission.
>   (!inline && triggerElement != null && inputElement == null);
> ```

That makes perfect sense !!. 
Separating the layout/focus flag from the native form ownership makes the intent much clearer. 

I'll revert `inputInsidePopup` to keep the PR scope small and rename the new state to `inputOwnsFormValue` as you suggested. I also reused `inputOwnsFormValue` in the input's name branch to keep the same concept in one place. 

Updating the PR shortly! Thanks for the review.
